items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: Oh, the leader was named George Morris, a trombone player, and a trumpet player was named Thomas Mack.

ctx.x: Who did you say was in that band?
Oh, the leader was named George Morris, a trombone player, and a trumpet player was named Thomas Mack. And Edmund Washington. We all had, we were taking lessons from this, Sam, for the Perkins. Yeah.
Oh, you were all taking lessons together?

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: we left here with with Joy Morris on trombone the manager and Mack on trumpet the leader and Edmund Washington on clarinet and me on banjo

ctx.x: Joe Strada yeah had him on drum that's right I had him straight that's right that was Prince Morris' band you see now Joe Wynn he brought us up there and he stole Albert Morgan and Edmund Hall out of that band and put them with the band we had and then the band we had when we left here we left here with with Joy Morris on trombone the manager and Mack on trumpet the leader and Edmund Washington on clarinet and me on banjo Joe Wynn that's full fine right there what happened to Edmund Washington? well he was still…

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1979-12-05
items.q: The Trammer played George Morris, and Trump was played Thomas Mack. And the saxophone player, Edmund Washington. I just buried them this year, first part of this year. And they used to get a little job, they used to hire me.

ctx.x: When did you start playing music professionally for, you know, your first few jobs?

Well I wasn't calling myself a professional before, before 24. I was in ninth grade, 35, right there, F1-0. And these two guys was taking lessons. This man and these guys were married men and everything. They left in the days first. The Trammer played George Morris, and Trump was played Thomas Mack. And the saxophone player, Edmund Washington. I just buried them this year, first part of this year. And they used to get a little job, they used to hire me. They had family and everything. I mean, they were work guys,…
Yeah. So you decided pretty much in Pensacola that, or?
